## Interview

**Q.** Tell me about your role in the landscaping partnership.

**A.** My brother and I each own half. I run the crews most of the week — it's my main job, the clinic desk is the steady paycheck.

**Q.** So you materially participated in the landscaping partnership during 2025?

**A.** Yes — several hundred hours; I'm on job sites almost every week of the season.

**Q.** You also have an S-corporation K-1 from Cedar & Vine Hospitality. What is that?

**A.** A little catering company a friend and I started — I own 40% and work the weekend events, so I'm hands-on there too, not just an investor.

**Q.** And the Northside Solar Partners K-1 — do you work in that one?

**A.** No, that one's purely money. I bought a 3% limited-partner stake in a solar fund; I don't run anything, I just get the K-1 each year. Passive, as I understand it.

**Q.** Did any of the three entities pay you cash distributions, or show amounts in boxes other than box 1 — interest, rental, guaranteed payments, section 179?

**A.** No distributions and no other boxes — just the box 1 income on each. The landscaping K-1 left my profit in the company; the accountants keep all three simple.

**Q.** You had only $2,140 withheld at the clinic. Did you make estimated tax payments toward the K-1 income?

**A.** No — I know that means I'll owe with the return. I've been setting money aside for the April payment.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind, disabled, or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No dependents, nobody can claim me, none of those apply, and yes — citizen all year.
